pick.headline: Bosnia votes on independence
pick.summary: On February 29 and March 1, 1992, Bosnia-Hercegovina held a referendum on independence; Bosnian Serbs boycotted it and the vote was overwhelmingly in favor.
pick.significance: Barricades went up in Sarajevo as results came in, and war began within weeks.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of March 3, 1992, led its front page with Zagreb radio: turnout in Bosnia-Hercegovina's independence referendum was 56.31 percent, enough for validity, while the Serbian Democratic Party claimed the barricades thrown up across Sarajevo to hinder the vote.

alternates.headline: Pierre Trudeau announces retirement
alternates.summary: On February 29, 1984, Canadian Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau announced that he would retire, after a walk in a snowstorm.
alternates.significance: Trudeau had spent his last months on a personal peace initiative between East and West.
alternates.fbis: The Soviet Union contents for March 1984 listed, at the end of its United States & Canada heading, "Canada's Trudeau Announces Plan To Resign", among Moscow commentaries on Reagan and U.S. defense spending.

alternates.headline: Siege of Sarajevo formally ends
alternates.summary: On February 29, 1996, the Bosnian government declared the siege of Sarajevo officially over, as Serb-held suburbs passed to federation control under the Dayton agreement.
alternates.significance: The siege had lasted nearly four years, the longest of a capital city in modern warfare.
alternates.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of March 1, 1996, carried Bosnian Serb SRNA and Sarajevo television items as Serb-held suburbs changed hands: Serbs said to be leaving Serb Sarajevo, a Serb Radical leader urging a hard inter-entity border, and federation assurances to Serbs in Ilijas.
